title: Bram and the Language
premise: Emrys Eriksen, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost her sense of taste after her mother's death, returns to the coastal town of Vell when the house she grew up in is auctioned by the family that took her in. There she finds an unfinished manuscript in her mother's hand—a single untranslatable sentence in a dying dialect, left untranslated since the night Emrys's father was wrongly accused of theft and driven from town. As Emrys works to decode the sentence with the help of Halvard, the auctioneer's son and her childhood accomplice, she uncovers proof that the town's beloved patriarch committed the crime, forcing her to choose between exposing a truth that will shatter the community that sheltered her or preserving the lie that gave her a home. In the end she publishes the translation alongside her final review—her first honest words about taste—and leaves Vell owning herself at last, though not the house.
about_author: Orsen Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing other people's confessions before writing fiction of his own. He lives above a shuttered bakery on the northern coast, where he collects dictionaries of extinct languages.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys reviews a tasting menu she cannot taste, writing luminous prose from memory and technique alone. A letter arrives: the Eriksen house in Vell goes to auction in six weeks. Emotional beat: hollow competence—the reader sees a woman performing life fluently while feeling nothing.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She returns to Vell incognito and walks the property at dusk, remembering how her mother spoke a private dialect with old Marta Bram, for whom the house's garden gate still bears a carved word no one could read. Beat: grief resurfacing as physical sensation.

chapters.title: The Auctioneer's Son
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Halvard Nystrom recognizes her at the preview viewing; their shared childhood complicity—he covered for her thefts of orchard fruit—rekindles wary intimacy. He warns her the Nystrom family expects to buy the house cheaply. Beat: belonging offered with strings attached.

chapters.title: What Marta Left
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the attic she finds her mother's notebook: recipes interleaved with dialect phrases, ending in one long untranslated sentence dated the week her father fled. Beat: discovery that reframes her mother's silence as protection, not coldness.

chapters.title: A Justice of Small Accounts
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. Halvard recalls the trial-by-gossip that ruined Erik Eriksen: missing silver, a patriarch's certainty, a town eager to believe. His father's ledgers show payments he was never meant to see. Beat: loyalty to family beginning to curdle into doubt.

chapters.title: The Dying Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She tracks down Marta Bram's granddaughter, Signe, last fluent speaker, who agrees to work through the sentence but demands Emrys explain why it matters. Halfway through, Signe stops: the sentence names who really took the silver. Beat: truth within reach and terrifying.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. Halvard confronts his dying grandfather, who neither confesses nor denies, only says the town needed someone guilty. Halvard copies the ledger pages, betraying blood for justice. Beat: the cost of loyalty vs. truth made explicit.

chapters.title: Six Weeks, Then None
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The auction accelerates; a developer outbids everyone's expectations, and Emrys realizes the house—and the sentence—will be sealed away forever unless she acts now. Signe completes the translation and hands it over like something hot. Beat: rising panic, point of no return.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Sentence
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the auction itself, with Halvard beside her, Emrys stands and reads the translated sentence aloud: her mother's testimony naming old Nystrom, and forgiving him anyway. The room fractures; the sale collapses into chaos. Climax: truth spoken outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Owning the Taste
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Weeks later, Emrys publishes her final review—an essay on the sentence, the silver, and the first meal she has truly tasted in years, cooked in Signe's kitchen. She lets the house go to the town as a reading room. Resolution: she leaves invisible no longer, carrying language instead of walls.
